# Resources for Teaching and Research

To get started in the Institute, you can familiarize yourself with the resources available for helping you teach and conduct research effectively. The [Academic Rules](#sec:acadrules) discuss all aspects related to courses, curricula and other teaching related aspects and [Resources for Teaching](#sec:teachingresources) lists some resources to help with teaching. The Institute, while encouraging you to apply for external grants to support your research, also provides you a Seed grant to get you started on your research projects. More details on this are available [here](#sec:researchfunding). You also have access to a Research and Development Fund (RDF) that can be used with more flexibility for your research related activities. Your academic unit would also have a Department Development Fund to support development activities of interest to your academic unit as a whole. These are discussed in greater detail [here](#sec:rdfddf).

In addition to research projects, one may also take on [consultancy projects](consultancy.qmd) for external organizations. Finally, the [Continuing Education Programme (CEP)](#sec:cep) permits you to conduct courses for external organizations through the Institute.

## Computing, storage and writing tools

- *Google Workspace:* the Computer Centre provides Google Workspace for
  Education Plus, with 500 GB of Drive storage per faculty member, Meet
  with up to 1000 participants and recording, and originality reports
  for plagiarism checks.
- *OneDrive:* the faculty quota is 10 GB. Move large files elsewhere. In
  January 2026 the Computer Centre advised keeping backups of
  OneDrive, Exchange and SharePoint data outside the @iitb.ac.in Microsoft
  tenant, as Microsoft had made the tenant read-only.
- *High performance computing:* the Computer Centre's clusters include
  Praganak. Request an account at
  [hpcaccreq.iitb.ac.in](https://hpcaccreq.iitb.ac.in).
- *Library tools:* the Central Library provides Turnitin, Grammarly and
  Overleaf. With an Overleaf faculty licence you can add any number of
  students to your projects.

## Publishing

Write the Institute's address in all publications as: Laboratory/
Department/Centre/Unit, Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Powai,
Mumbai - 400076. Do not abbreviate the name to IIT Bombay or IITB, or add
punctuation to it.

From 19 September 2026, corresponding authors at IIT Bombay can publish
open access without article processing charges in eligible Cambridge
University Press journals, under a one-year agreement with the Central
Library.

Under One Nation One Subscription (ONOS), authors can apply for support
with article processing charges in listed journals through the [ONOS
portal](https://www.onos.gov.in/apc-support). Use your @iitb.ac.in email
address and your correct affiliation.
